newsitem.title: UK: World tin prices at lowest for six months.
newsitem.headline: World tin prices at lowest for six months.

text.p: Three months tin futures on the London Metal Exchange (LME) fell to the lowest level for more than six months, hitting $6,050 a tonne.
This was down $50 from Friday's close and below key support of $6,060 a tonne with the losses a reflection of overall bearish sentiment still swamping the base metals complex.

On Monday the Association of Tin Producing Countries (ATPC) started a two-day ministerial conference in Singapore. The group has aimed to support prices through production quotas, but these were being increasingly ignored by members.

Also helping to weigh on market sentiment was an estimate ahead of the meeting by Miguel Navarrede-Fernandez, general director of Brazil's Ministry of Mines and Energy, that world stocks of tin would have risen to 36,000 tonnes at the end of 1996 from 30,000 at the end of 1995.
The group was also was hit by the defection of two members, Australia and Thailand, last week.
The next downside target for tin was pegged by technical analysts at $5,970.
